sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III Black Holes, University of Cambridge lecture notes (2024)

contents.name: §10.8, equations (10.110)–(10.112): stationary area coefficient and units

source_review.read_extent: Fetched the complete 149-page lecture-notes PDF and read §10.8, including the mechanical first-law form, the area coefficient in natural units, and its SI reinstatement.
source_review.supports: The optional area summand has the familiar SI coefficient k_B c^3/(4 G hbar), used here only as a declared model summand.
source_review.limitations: The notes' formula concerns stationary Einstein black-hole thermodynamics. It does not establish a regulator-dependent G_Lambda formula on an arbitrary fixed background.

source_review.read_extent: Read the full section on the generalized-entropy summary and its preceding area and Hawking-radiation discussion.
source_review.supports: The outside-matter contribution is distinct from the black-hole area term in the summarized generalized entropy.
source_review.limitations: The lecture-note summary does not spell out hypotheses for a general monotonicity theorem. It is used as context only; Wall's full conditional proof and the local item scope retain the necessary qualifications.

source_review.read_extent: Read the full discussion immediately following the generalized-entropy summary and the evaporation estimate.
source_review.supports: A fixed-background entropy definition does not by itself include the effect of emitted radiation on the spacetime geometry.
source_review.limitations: The lecture notes give only a qualitative backreaction boundary here; no backreaction claim is included in the assigned definition.

sources.title: Aron C. Wall, A proof of the generalized second law for rapidly changing fields and arbitrary horizon slices, Physical Review D 85, 104049 (2012), arXiv:1105.3445v6

contents.name: §1, equations (1)–(3): horizon and outside entropy terms and UV divergence

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete introductory discussion of S_H+S_out, the finite-regulator notation boundary, and the stated ultraviolet divergence of exterior entanglement entropy.
source_review.supports: The geometric and outside terms are separate inputs, and a renormalized generalized entropy requires an explicit prescription for the divergent outside contribution.
source_review.limitations: Wall's article uses a semiclassical QFT setting and does not establish the finite-matrix definition or convergence of this item's chosen sequence.

contents.name: §§2.1–2.8: conditional GSL proof and renormalization conditions

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete proof route: semiclassical Einstein assumptions, horizon-algebra axioms, the relative-entropy monotonicity argument, the outside-region extension, and the full renormalization discussion.
source_review.supports: A physical generalized-second-law conclusion uses a specified state evolution, horizon geometry, field-algebra assumptions, and an additional renormalized relative-entropy/free-energy relation.
source_review.limitations: Wall's proof is conditional and its renormalized relation is explicitly assumed in the article; its conclusion is not transferred to arbitrary finite-regulator data or to every gravity/matter model.
